content: The vscode extension features the extremely useful but little known action called Lean 4: Project: Fetch Mathlib Build Cache For Current Imports (accessible from the command palette via Ctrl + Shift + P or Cmd + Shift + P). After having used it for more than a year, there are several improvements that come to mind.

First, I often find myself wanting to run this action for five or so files (which is still faster than running lake exe cache get since the files together import a tiny fraction of mathlib). Right now, I need to repeatedly wait for the previous run of the action to be over to start one on a new file, because the action doesn't want to run concurrently to the server restarting.

I see an obvious solution to this problem, namely to make the action fetch cache for all open files rather than the single focused file. If implemented, I suggest renaming the action to Lean 4: Project: Fetch Mathlib Build Cache For Open Files

Second, it would be valuable to be able to run the action downstream of mathlib. I understand that it cannot work upstream of it because cache has yet to be integrated to core, but I see no reason why it cannot work downstream: lake exe cache get Module.Name works just fine in downstream projects after all.
Finally, given how useful and unknown the action is, I recommend that it figures much more prominently, eg as a button next to the Restart File one in the infoview.

Yaël Dillies said:

I see an obvious solution to this problem, namely to make the action fetch cache for all open files rather than the single focused file. If implemented, I suggest renaming the action to Lean 4: Project: Fetch Mathlib Build Cache For Open Files

Sounds reasonable to me.

Generally, people sometimes accumulate hundreds of Lean tabs over time that they've forgotten about, and I suspect that not everyone would want to fetch the cache for all tabs, but we can easily add a quick pick dialog that just defaults to all open files and lets users quickly reduce the selection (i.e. it's just one additional input of 'Enter' in your workflow). Does that sound good to you?

Marc Huisinga said:

I suspect that not everyone would want to fetch the cache for all tabs

That's what I thought too, but then I realised this was never worse than lake exe cache get, which people are generally happy to do. I would therefore avoid the extra dialog unless people complain
Regarding the interaction of my first and third suggestions, if we acquire a button, it should probably only fetch cache for the focused file, to match the behavior of the Restart File button

I have recently added a keyboard shortcut for this command, and I find it very useful. I agree it would be nice to have a command that gets cache for all open files, but I would like to keep the command that does it only for the current file (otherwise I'll be closing files that I'd otherwise want to keep open)

vscode-lean4#757

Yaël Dillies said:

Finally, given how useful and unknown the action is, I recommend that it figures much more prominently, eg as a button next to the Restart File one in the infoview.

I'd like to avoid us adding more buttons like the 'Restart File' one to the InfoView. I suspect most users are perfectly fine with just fetching the entire cache pre-hoc, as you say :-)
That said, we'll likely re-think some of the UI-related aspects of caching once the new cache is being used.
